name: Short Put Butterfly
summary: Sell 1 higher put, buy 2 body puts, sell 1 lower put for a credit; the put-side mirror of the short call butterfly, profiting on a move out of the tent.
when_to_use: Same as the short call butterfly: IV rank < 25 plus a dated catalyst. Choose the put version when put skew makes the credit larger for the same three strikes; compare both and take the bigger credit.
max_loss: width - net credit at the body. Defined.
breakevens: lower breakeven = lower strike + credit; upper breakeven = upper strike - credit
entry_rules: IV rank < 25 and a dated catalyst inside the expiry.
Equal wings; OI >= 500 and per-leg spread <= max($0.05, 10% of mid).
Single multi-leg limit order at mid, accept mid - $0.02.
management_rules: Close at 50% of the credit captured.
Close the session after the catalyst resolves regardless of P/L.
Hard stop at 2.0x the credit in mark-to-market loss.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: two short put strikes exist; flatten the entire structure by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close immediately if either short put is ITM with extrinsic < $0.10.
assignment_risk: Two short put strikes. The upper short put is ITM in the winning downside scenario, and assignment means buying 100 shares per contract at that strike - on a $600 ETF that is $60,000 of stock against a $50k account. Early assignment risk rises as extrinsic decays toward zero.
common_mistakes: Same as the short call butterfly, plus underestimating the cash impact of a short put assignment on a large-notional ETF.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended for the same reasons as the short call butterfly.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
